problem: The shared app stylesheet historically used generic structural class names such as .nav for archive-explorer layout while static reader pages reused the same names for unrelated page-local elements. In particular, .nav meant both sticky archive sidebar and horizontal page links, producing overlapping header/title layers.
decision: Structural layout ownership is now explicit and namespaced. Semantic HTML elements such as nav may be reused, but a generic CSS class may not own unrelated layouts across presentation systems.

layers.name: site shell
layers.rule: Global site identity/navigation shell only. Sticky behavior is allowed only on explicitly named shell components.

layers.name: page navigation
layers.rule: Normal document flow. Never inherits archive-sidebar sticky positioning.

layers.name: page intro
layers.rule: Normal document flow beneath page navigation. No negative overlap with site shell or navigation.

layers.name: page content
layers.rule: A static page owns its own content layout; shared archive grid/sidebar rules cannot leak into it.

layers.name: archive explorer
layers.rule: Interactive archive-only structure. Sticky sidebar and archive grid behavior must be scoped here.

layers.name: specialized modules
layers.rule: Timeline and future modules use unique prefixes; they do not claim generic site classes.

migration_rule: Existing reader pages are protected by app/layout-guard.css. When an old page is next edited, migrate its structural class to page-* naming instead of adding z-index or spacing hacks.
runtime_rule: app/reader.css imports app/layout-guard.css so shared-style static pages remain safe before individual markup migration.
test_rule: scripts/check_css_namespace_collisions.py is the automated regression check and is run by .github/workflows/css-namespace-check.yml.
definition_of_fixed: A page header bug is fixed only when ownership/scope prevents collision at all viewport sizes and content lengths. Increasing margins, adding arbitrary z-index, or moving one heading is not considered a permanent fix.
